A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of Conformal Prediction for Hierarchical Data, with matching authors, framework and core theoretical results. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support a reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original simulations and analysis of Palo Alto electric-vehicle charging demand, including coverage and interval-length results in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: V3 reports original simulations evaluating component-wise prediction across six hierarchical configurations and joint prediction on two configurations, with numerical results in Section 5 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The reconciliation-plus-SCP framework remains, including joint prediction already described in v2 Appendix E. V3 corrects the written output of the hierarchical joint algorithm: Algorithm 2 centers its ellipsoid on the projected regressor, whereas v2 Algorithm 5 used the unprojected regressor in its output formula despite calibrating projected residuals.

E1.justification: The Palo Alto charging-demand application and original eight-node simulation are removed. V3 evaluates component-wise prediction on six synthetic hierarchies with 16–1,801 nodes and depths three or four, and adds joint-coverage evaluation on the two smallest configurations.

E2.justification: Direct, OLS, WLS, Combi and MinT remain the practical component-wise comparison set. Oracle MinT disappears with the Palo Alto experiment. The new joint-coverage experiments evaluate plain ellipsoidal SCP against its reconciled counterpart; v2 described these methods theoretically without reporting this comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix F changes the synthetic sample size from 100,000 to 1,000,000, feature means from (1, 0, -1) to (10, -5, 5), noise covariance construction, and full-feature availability probability from 0.7 to 0.8. The 40/20/20/20 split proportions remain. New joint experiments introduce normalized-volume evaluation and three norm-matrix choices.

E4.justification: V3 adds analyses of performance across hierarchy sizes and depths, sensitivity to the joint-prediction norm matrix, and component-wise behavior in the new configurations. V2's real-data diagnostics—Student-density fits, Q-Q plots and estimated-versus-oracle covariance comparisons in Appendix F.2—are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions use 1,000 simulation runs and 95% confidence margins. For total lengths, v2 Equation (21) transforms interval endpoints as sqrt(L minus gamma) and sqrt(L plus gamma); v3 Equation (20) substitutes wider symmetric intervals, sqrt(L) plus or minus sqrt(gamma). This changes uncertainty construction without establishing an increased repeated-run count.

E6.justification: The original synthetic and Palo Alto results are replaced by results under different hierarchies and generative settings. V3's configuration 5 reports total-length estimates of 10,424 for Direct, 8,861 for WLS and 10,613 for MinT. Its new joint results include normalized volumes of 17.4 versus 16.5 for plain versus reconciled SCP in configuration 1. These are new comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The main elliptical-distribution and trace-minimization results remain. V2 Theorem E.3's set-inclusion guarantee becomes the volume inequality in v3 Theorem 5, with reasoning that explicitly accommodates different ellipsoid centers. Coverage statements also revise their conditions to refer explicitly to projected scores. These are substantive corrections within the existing theory.

C1.justification: V2's abstract and outline claim empirical illustration on artificial and real data; v3 limits that support to simulations across hierarchy scales. V3 also foregrounds the existing joint-coverage contribution. The central claims of combining conformal prediction with reconciliation and establishing efficiency guarantees remain.

C2.justification: V3 shifts practical advice from v2's synthetic-data preference for MinT toward WLS, adding a near-singular-covariance hypothesis for large-hierarchy failures. Sections 1.1, 4.1 and 6 substantially expand discussion of elliptical assumptions, time dependence and applicability limits. However, its broad claim that MinT underperforms Direct on the largest hierarchies overstates the table: configuration 6 reports 10,503 for MinT versus 10,621 for Direct.

D1.justification: Appendix F substantially revises the reproduction instructions for the new hierarchies and data generators. V3 newly documents computing resources and runtimes, fixed GAM penalties through sp=1, bam with discrete=TRUE, and Moore-Penrose inverse conventions. V2's detailed Palo Alto preprocessing, forecasting and oracle-estimation instructions are removed.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning around conformal efficiency guarantees, discussing Burnaev and Vovk, Bars and Humbert, and Henderson et al. It adds optimal-transport approaches, hierarchical classification distinctions and adaptive conformal work for future time-series extensions. The electric-vehicle application references disappear, while the central forecast-reconciliation lineage remains.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten into motivation, related work, contributions and outline subsections. Joint and component-wise objectives receive separate treatments, a discussion section is added, and the appendices are reordered to place efficiency proofs before coverage proofs. Algorithm terminology and explanatory passages are revised throughout.

P2.justification: V3 replaces the two-column main-text layout with a single-column format and reformats algorithm boxes and the method-summary table. The main experimental plots become numerical tables; the real-data diagnostic figures disappear. New hierarchy diagrams, an explanatory uncertainty graphic and redesigned component-wise plots substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 improves correctness by aligning the reconciled ellipsoid's center with its calibration scores and replacing the inconsistent construction and inclusion claim with an appropriate volume comparison. Broader robustness evidence, implementation details and clearer applicability limits also help. These gains are tempered by removal of the sole real-data study and the overgeneralized MinT-failure interpretation, supporting a limited net improvement.
